title: Data in support of proteomic analysis of the PJI cohort PRIS
projectDescription: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a debilitating and dangerous pathology following joint arthroplasty procedures. With increasing incidence of arthroplasty procedures, the burden of PJI is expected to continually grow. A correct and early diagnosis of PJI, proves difficult, with the lack of an available single standardized molecular test. The utilization of serology-based biomarkers would provide a non-invasive sampling method, however, these methods are especially deficient in the diagnostic criteria. The aim of the present study was to employ liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry-based (LC-MS) techniques to explore the proteomic profile of plasma samples derived from a Danish PJI cohort, PRIS, to better elucidate relevant proteins separating PJI patients from patients experiencing aseptic failure (AF) and chronic pain.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Blood plasma samples was obtained from patients enrolled in the multidisciplinary Prosthetic-Related-Infection and Pain (Danish acronym, PRIS) study, conducted in the North Denmark Region. MS-based proteomic profiling was performed using a bottom-up approach utilizing a standard protein aggregation capture (PAC) MS preparatory method. Blood plasma samples were digested with trypsin using an automated Opentrons OT-2 liquid handling system and analyzed by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) on a timsTOF Pro2 mass spectrometer (Bruker, DE) coupled to an EvosepONE system (Evosep, DK) using 60SPD and Evosep performance column (EV1115). Data-independent acquisition (DIA-PASEF) was employed for peptide fragmentation.
dataProcessingProtocol: Protein identification and quantification were conducted via Spectronaut v19.5 (Biognosys, Switcherland) against the UniProt human reference proteome (May, 2025). Data structure and naming is available from excel file in the Pride archive.
